inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (721.787M), rounded to 722.0M. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; buybacks ($160M FY2025, $20M H1 2026 under the new $1B authorization) are the mechanism that keeps it flat.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation, FY2025 10-K cash flow statement ($43M; FY2024 $43M). No separately disclosed equity-award withholding tax line post-FY2015; immaterial.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 -> cost of equity ~9.3%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (weighted-average coupon cut >130bp since 2022) with little tax shield because most interest sits at the REIT level. Market weights ~72% equity / 28% debt -> WACC ~8.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: housing-cycle risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not via a discount-rate premium (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost already sits inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA; the small finance-lease balance is inside total_debt. One treatment, no adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: owner-FCF component DCF (unlevered, mid-cycle) with the cyclical adaptations, NOT REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity. The routing table's REIT row is for IAS-40 fair-value property trusts whose flow is a post-interest AFFO; WY is a historical-cost timber REIT whose largest segment (Wood Products, ~70% of sales) is a taxable-REIT-subsidiary commodity manufacturer. EBITDA, capex and net debt all mean what the engine assumes, so the business straddles the 'REIT' and 'cyclical operating company' rows and the operating route is the one whose inputs exist. Flows are pre-interest; net debt ($5,303M debt less $527M cash, 30 Jun 2026) is deducted once in the bridge -- never capitalise FAD at CoE and also deduct debt. CAPEX: the CSV CapEx/FCF columns are blank from FY2019 (XBRL tag change); capex here is us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentAdditions ($474M FY2025) plus PaymentsForCapitalImprovements, the timberland reforestation line ($51M) = $525M (7.6% of sales). Timberland acquisitions ($469M FY2025) are treated as land-portfolio recycling funded by divestitures and excluded from both capex and revenue growth. Capex steady-state below D&A is deliberate: ~40% of D&A is timber depletion, whose replacement is reforestation, already in capex. FY0 OWNER FCF: OCF $562M - capex $525M - SBC $43M = -$6M; that figure is post-interest ($272M paid) and FY2025 is a housing-trough year (EBITDA margin 18.0% vs ~25% 2017-2025 average), so the projection is built from components on a mid-cycle margin path, not from last_fcf. Cash tax: REIT-level timber income untaxed; TRS (Wood Products) taxed -- cash taxes were 9% of EBIT in FY2025 and ~17-18% at the FY2021-22 peak, so the rate rises with Wood Products' share of profit. SBC: 0.6% of sales, house and street nearly coincide. Q2 2026 EBITDA includes a $71M timberland-divestiture gain; the FY2026 margin anchor strips it. Dividend ~$0.84/yr (75-80% of Adjusted FAD payout framework) is a distribution of these flows, not an addition to them.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All 3- and 5-year CAGRs are cycle artefacts: they run from the FY2021-22 lumber super-cycle peak (EBITDA margin 35-40%) to the FY2024-25 housing trough (17-18%). Equity CAGR (+1.5% 5yr) diverges by >30% from EPS (-15.9%) and revenue (-1.7%). The 10-year revenue CAGR is used as the growth anchor instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: FY2025 owner FCF is ~-$6M (trough, post-interest), so any CAGR ending there is undefined. FY2022 owner FCF was ~$2.28B (OCF 2,832 - capex 521 - SBC 33). Per-share history is only comparable post-FY2016 (Plum Creek merger 510M -> 749M shares).

base.narrative: Housing grinds back to trend by FY2028-29; margin reaches a 23.5% mid-cycle level (~2017-2025 average ex the 2021-22 spike), i.e. roughly half of management's $1.5B incremental-EBITDA roadmap is delivered.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 elevated by ~$300M Monticello EWP build (H1 2026 capex $282M); tapers after the H1 2027 start-up to ~6% (5.2% mill capex + 0.8% reforestation).
base.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: 16x terminal owner FCF: below the 18.6x Gordon value at 8%/2.5%, above the 12-15x cyclical default because ~10M acres of perpetual, inflation-linked timberland sit behind the Timberlands/SLS half of the flow.

bull.narrative: Rates ease and single-family starts re-accelerate from FY2027; lumber/EWP realizations normalise upward, OSB oversupply clears, Monticello and the Natural Climate Solutions/biocarbon/CCS pipeline scale -- most of the $1.5B roadmap lands and margin settles at 28%. Higher Wood Products profit lifts the TRS cash tax rate to 15%.

bear.narrative: Housing stays 'stuck in second gear' through the decade with mortgage rates in the mid-6s; OSB overcapacity is structural, lumber curtailment rallies fade, and SLS stays lumpy around ~$400-450M as large easements fail to recur. Margin only edges to 19%, roughly the FY2024-25 trough plus cost savings.

scenario_narratives.base: Housing grinds back toward trend by FY2028-29 on demographic undersupply; lumber normalises, OSB stays mediocre, Monticello EWP starts in H1 2027, and Strategic Land Solutions holds ~$450M EBITDA with Climate Solutions growing. EBITDA margin recovers from ~18.5% to a 23.5% mid-cycle level -- about half of management's $1.5B incremental-EBITDA roadmap. Capex tapers from the Monticello peak to ~6% of sales.
scenario_narratives.bull: Mortgage rates fall and single-family starts re-accelerate from 2027; lumber and EWP realizations reset higher, OSB oversupply clears, and the natural-climate pipeline (carbon credits, biocarbon with Aymium, CCS leasing, solar/wind, data-centre sites) scales. Most of the $1.5B roadmap lands, margin reaches 28%, and the market capitalises the timberland-backed flow at a higher exit multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Affordability keeps starts near 1.4M through the decade, OSB overcapacity proves structural, lumber rallies are curtailment-driven and fade, and SLS earnings stay lumpy because large conservation easements do not recur. Margin stalls near 19%, leverage stays ~4x EBITDA, and the base dividend is funded but buybacks stop.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the recovery's timing is unknowable, OSB oversupply is industry-wide, and SLS depends on episodic land deals -- but timberland asset backing and no near-term maturities rule out a solvency tail. Base 50%: a slow return to mid-cycle is the most likely path for a housing undersupplied market. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs rates, OSB and the climate businesses to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF. The latest owner FCF (~-$6M) is a housing-trough, post-interest number and is not projected; flows are rebuilt from a revenue path and a component margin build that recovers to a mid-cycle EBITDA margin. Net debt is deducted once. The REIT status shows up as a low cash tax rate on the timber half of the flow, not as a switch to AFFO-at-CoE capitalisation.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin assumption (23.5% base): each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly $1/share.
Terminal multiple: the timberland asset base argues for more than a cyclical 12-15x; the cap chosen (16x base) carries a large share of value.
Timberland is carried at historical cost; a private-market acreage NAV may exceed this flow-based value, and the DCF does not capture it as a separate asset.
Lumpy SLS land/conservation sales can swing any single year by $50-100M of EBITDA.

Capex history after FY2018 comes from XBRL tags outside the CSV (PropertyPlantAndEquipmentAdditions + PaymentsForCapitalImprovements); if reforestation is double-counted in the first tag, capex is overstated by ~0.7% of sales.
